raw_response:
I have 10.1 mu of land here in Quzhou County, and I have been working it for 45 years. My family has six mouths, but my son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in Handan, so it is mostly me and my wife handling the fields, with my younger brother helping during harvest. I do wheat-maize double cropping on all 10.1 mu. That is what every family around here does, and I am not about to change it.

This year, for the winter wheat, I sowed an improved variety I got from the seed dealer in town — it is the same one my neighbor Lao Wang used last year and he got over 1100 jin per mu. I put down seed at about 25 jin per mu. For fertilizer, I am not cutting corners. Last year fertilizer prices were high, but I still used 100 jin of 16-16-16 compound fertilizer per mu as base dressing at sowing time, and I will topdress another 100 jin of urea per mu when the wheat turns green in March. I know that is a lot, but I would rather waste a bag of fertilizer than lose a bag of grain. A bad harvest means I lose thousands of yuan; an extra bag of urea is only 100 yuan. So that comes to about 30 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus 8 kg of phosphorus and 8 kg of potassium. I worked it out with the dealer once. I till the ground with the rotary tiller before sowing wheat — I have been doing that for ten years now.

For water, I irrigate the wheat four times: once after sowing to help it settle before winter, once when it wakes up in spring, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The well water is there, and diesel for the pump costs money, but dry wheat means shriveled grain. I will spray pesticides three times: herbicide in early spring, then two more times for aphids and rust around April and May.

I expect my wheat to yield about 550 kg per mu. Last year I got 530 kg because of a dry April. If the rain is good this year, maybe 600 kg, but I budget for 550 kg.

After we harvest the wheat in early June, I plant hybrid maize the same day. There is no time to waste — if you wait three days, you lose a week of growing season. I use a no-till seeder now. I switched five years ago after watching Lao Zhang do it. It saves me diesel and one pass over the field. I plant about 3 jin of hybrid seed per mu. 

For the maize, I put 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu in the row at planting, and then I topdress 70 jin of urea per mu when the maize is knee-high. That is about 24 kg of nitrogen per mu, 8 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium. I give it two irrigations: one right after planting if the soil is dry, and one big one at the trumpet stage. If July is very hot, maybe a third, but twice is usually enough. I spray twice for pests: herbicide right after planting, and once for corn borer when the tassels start showing.

I expect the maize to give me 620 kg per mu. The hybrid seed is good stuff. Two years ago I got 650 kg, last year 600 kg. 620 kg is a honest number.

My family needs this income. Even with my son sending money home, we still pay for my granddaughter's school. I spend roughly 650 yuan per mu on the wheat for fertilizer, seed, pesticide, and diesel, and about 550 yuan per mu on the maize. I do not like spending that much, but I know that if I go cheap, the yield drops faster than the costs do.
